Binning affects appearance; a distribution alone does not demonstrate diagnostic value.

aggregate.title: Source definitions/provenance
aggregate.explanation: Essence of This Table  Source definitions and provenance explain which dataset, eligibility rules and reference classifications support these loaded analyses. Check them before interpreting the outputs; metadata do not certify original clinical records.

Inspect typical costs, variation and group size before judging the financial difference. This is observational total expenditure, not itemised pathway cost or a causal severity effect.

Read complicated-minus-simple effects and intervals in NGN alongside the actual rank or Welch result. Statistical significance is not a causal cost driver, savings estimate or cost-effectiveness conclusion.

aggregate.title: Cost distribution comparison
aggregate.explanation: Essence of This Figure  The box plot shows how recorded hospital costs vary and overlap between simple and complicated histology. Median and spread reveal features hidden by a single group average; the adjacent test informs the comparison. Whiskers show observed extremes; the visual difference does not establish causation or savings from a diagnostic strategy.

aggregate.title: Diagnostic estimates
aggregate.explanation: Essence of This Table  A useful diagnostic approach must identify appendicitis while also recognising its absence against histopathology. Read sensitivity and specificity together, with their denominators and uncertainty, rather than choosing a method from accuracy alone. High disease prevalence can make accuracy look high even when specificity is poor; rates alone do not prove one method is superior.

aggregate.title: Paired raw-marker comparisons
aggregate.explanation: Essence of This Table  Comparing markers on the same participants preserves the paired study design. DeLong addresses raw-marker ranking; stratified McNemar addresses discordant fixed classifications. Read the method before interpreting a p-value. These exploratory comparisons are unadjusted and do not test superiority of fitted combined models.

aggregate.title: Highest point estimates
aggregate.explanation: Essence of This Table  These rows identify the highest displayed point estimate for each selected diagnostic measure. Different measures answer different questions, so a leading point estimate is not a validated winner or evidence of superiority. Review intervals and evaluation methods in the full comparison.

aggregate.title: Selected diagnostic ROC curves
aggregate.explanation: Essence of This Figure  ROC curves make the trade-off between detecting disease and false-positive results visible as thresholds change. A curve’s shape shows ranking across thresholds; the declared operating-point table explains actual binary decisions. Visual separation is not a superiority test, and raw-marker curves and held-out model curves have different evaluation procedures.

aggregate.title: Selected model calibration plots
aggregate.explanation: Essence of This Figure  Calibration plots compare predicted probabilities with observed disease proportions. Agreement with the diagonal supports probability agreement within the plotted bins; inspect each bin’s size and interval. Sparse bins and internal validation limit precision; calibration does not measure clinical benefit.

aggregate.title: Pairwise associations
aggregate.explanation: Essence of This Table  The association table explores how recorded scores, biomarkers, costs and intervals vary together. Correlation direction and uncertainty indicate monotonic relationships; use the supplied Holm-adjusted p-values for this family. Association is not causation and does not establish an adjusted effect or clinical usefulness.

aggregate.title: Recorded-group comparisons
aggregate.explanation: Essence of This Table  The selected group comparisons ask whether the listed measurements differ across their recorded categories. Read each named comparison, effect, denominator and supplied adjustment together. Exploratory associations do not establish independent or causal effects.

aggregate.title: Selected association scatter
aggregate.explanation: Essence of This Figure  This scatter plot shows actual recorded pairs for the selected variables. Inspect direction, spread and unusual points with the corresponding correlation and interval. Neither the visual pattern nor correlation establishes causation.

aggregate.title: Selected group distributions
aggregate.explanation: Essence of This Figure  This plot shows the distribution and overlap of the selected recorded measurement across the selected groups. Read the medians and spread with the matching test, effect and intervals. Visual separation is not a causal explanation or proof of clinical importance.
